newsitem.title: FRANCE: MOTOR RACING-PROST TO LAUNCH OWN FORMULA ONE TEAM.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-PROST TO LAUNCH OWN FORMULA ONE TEAM.

text.p: Four times world champion Alain Prost has reached an agreement to take over Ligier and will launch a new Formula One team on Friday, L'Equipe said on Thursday.
Ligier will become Prost Grand Prix and contest the 1997 world championship with drivers Olivier Panis of France and Shinji Nakano of Japan, the newspaper added.
Prost will rely on the new Ligier JS 45 cars powered by a Mugen-Honda engine this season, but from 1998 his cars will be fitted with the Peugeot V10 engines currently used by Jordan.
Prost needed the agreement of all the existing teams to change the Ligier name but he had to wait until Wednesday to gain Jordan boss Eddie Jordan's signature, according to the newspaper.
Ligier, now owned by Benetton boss Flavio Briatore of Italy, was created in 1976 and scored nine grand prix wins, the last one by Panis in Monaco last year.
Prosot won a record 51 grands prix, the last in 1993. He lifted the drivers' world title in 1985, 1986, 1989 and 1993.
